extracted.intended_audience: authors and writers seeking representation (fiction and select nonfiction) querying Emily Sacks / CAA
extracted.subtask_description: A literary assistant's manuscript wish list and submission guidelines describing what fiction and select nonfiction they are actively seeking, with genre preferences, exemplar comps, and how to submit queries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall focus: fiction and select nonfiction
rubrics_metrics.description: I am a literary assistant at Creative Artists Agency building my own list. I am looking for fiction and select nonfiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary emphasis is on fiction; nonfiction consideration is selective (see 'Nonfiction: History' below).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fiction — Romance (contemporary, historical, paranormal, romantasy, 'booktok')
rubrics_metrics.description: Romance (contemporary, historical, paranormal, romantasy, “booktok”): THE PARADISE PROBLEM, THE HATING GAME, BRIDE, THE KNIGHT AND THE MOTH
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples provided as comps; open to a range of romance subgenres including booktok-friendly titles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fiction — Fantasy (high-fantasy, vast world-building, romantasy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fantasy (high-fantasy, vast world-building, romantasy): DEADLY EDUCATION, FOURTH WING, THE EMPRESS OF SALT AND FORTUNE, THE FAMILIAR, THRONE OF GLASS
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefers fantasy with expansive world-building and romantic elements; see also explicit note that 'any fantasy must have a strong foundation for its world building and setting.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Fiction — Sci‑Fi (space operas, space westerns)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sci-Fi (space operas, space westerns): A MEMORY CALLED EMPIRE, RENDEZVOUS WITH RAMA, THE TUSKS OF EXTINCTION, ROSE/HOUSE
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Looks for speculative fiction with big-scope, space-opera or space-western sensibilities; examples act as comps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fiction — Westerns (with a twist)
rubrics_metrics.description: Westerns (with a twist): THE COUNTRY UNDER HEAVEN, THE BULLET SWALLOWER
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wants westerns that have an unexpected or fresh angle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fiction — Fairy Tales / Folk Tales
rubrics_metrics.description: Fairy Tales/Folk Tales: THISTLEFOOT, HOW TO BE EATEN, SPINNING SILVER, THE NIGHT ENDS WITH FIRE, THE FOX WIFE
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interested in retellings or works rooted in folklore and fairy-tale traditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fiction — Horror
rubrics_metrics.description: Horror: THE UNWORTHY, THE STARVING SAINTS
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open to horror titles; examples show contemporary literary/speculative horror.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select short story collections
rubrics_metrics.guidance: She expresses interest in short story collections, especially those that tell under-represented stories (see related criterion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for under-represented stories
rubrics_metrics.description: I would love to see books that tell under-represented stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit preference for narratives that bring forward marginalized, overlooked, or less-represented perspectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical fiction expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Historical fiction should feel well-researched and authentic
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authenticity and solid research are required; historical voice and detail should convincingly evoke the period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fantasy world‑building requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Any fantasy must have a strong foundation for its world building and setting
rubrics_metrics.guidance: World-building must be thoughtful and plausible within the work's internal logic; setting should support stakes and character action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonfiction — History (approach)
rubrics_metrics.description: History (an emphasis on taking an event or singular topic and expanding on it)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interested in narrative/history projects that take a focused event or topic and expand it into a larger book-length treatment; examples include Cleopatra’s Daughter, In Search of Amrit Kaur, The Curse of the Marquis de Sade.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open to works comparible to Silvia Moreno‑Garcia
rubrics_metrics.description: I am open to anything that can be comped to the works of Silvia Moreno-Garcia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comps to Silvia Moreno-Garcia indicate interest in literary speculative works with strong voice, atmosphere, and possibly folkloric or historical elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vital genres / categories (representative list)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fiction: Commercial, Fantasy, Folklore, Gothic, Historical, Horror, Magical Realism, New Adult, Romance, Romcom, Science Fiction, Short Story, Speculative, Western, Women’s Fiction. Non-Fiction: History
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A consolidated list of genres and categories she represents or is actively seeking; use this as a quick reference to compatibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Desire: 'the next' Silvia Moreno‑Garcia; specific wish‑list hooks
rubrics_metrics.description: I’d like the next… Silvia Moreno-Garcia. Romance novel with realistic characters and untold stories. Authentic, awe-inspiring fantasy world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expresses concrete 'wish list' desiderata: literary/genre crossover work that captures the qualities of those prompts (realistic characters, untold stories, awe-inspiring, authentic worldbuilding).

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission guidelines — email + manuscript format
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions should be emailed to rafe.sagalynasst@caa.com. Please email your query and the first 50 pages of the manuscript pasted in the body of the email.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required submission format: query letter plus first 50 pages pasted directly into the email body (do not attach those pages). Use the provided email address; this is the preferred/only submission route specified on the page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact / vital info (assistant agent identity)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides the specific contact and role to direct submissions to; useful for addressing query and understanding submission recipient.
